title: Confidence Interval Length under Partial Interference with Unequal Clique Sizes
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier=incremental below floor=field; projected paper-score ceiling 6.4 < 7.4; salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: It does not prove the universal sharp confidence-length frontier: both the linear water-filling converse and the matching no-dominance lower bound remain open, so the general result is not a sharp minimax rate theorem.
The central implication from the outer posterior pieces to two target tails is asserted rather than derived.
Pairwise Hellinger control does not by itself prove the asserted posterior interval missed-mass event.
The central all-procedure confidence-length consistency boundary is not positioned against the accepted-bank closest experiment result exp_snipe_degree_frontier_v1.

The positioning does not give each cited item a relevance sentence: in particular KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024 and HarshawMiddletonSavje2021 appear in the bibliography but are absent from the substantive related-work comparison.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the exact categorical block reduction, sharpened finite and trimmed HT upper bounds, capped-modulus duality, a cubic all-procedure lower bound yielding the exact fixed-confidence consistency boundary, and a matching fixed-alpha rate for the constructed two-scale family. Two attempts at the advertised universal linear lower frontier failed at the same load-bearing posterior-spread step: weighted-Rademacher anti-concentration did not establish the required posterior quantile gap, while the smooth-location route did not control moving-support endpoints or convert Hellinger bounds into posterior interval spread. The surviving package is mathematically sound but incremental; both universal lower obligations remain open.
tldr: Unequal clique sizes turn full-neighborhood All Treat and All Control exposure into independent nonidentical categorical reveals. The exact centered block Horvitz--Thompson increment is at most \(w_l/(2q_l)\), giving the clipped half-width \(\sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}+M\log(2/\alpha)/6\). Trimming is within a factor \(5/2\) of the capped water-filling modulus and yields \(\mathcal R_\alpha\le5\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\). A cubic common-location lower bound proves the exact fixed-confidence consistency boundary, and a separate product-Rademacher argument gives \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) for the stated two-scale family. The sole unresolved sharp-frontier step is a universal linear weighted-erasure lower bound for all measurable externally randomized intervals. The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) diagnostic reports structural graph rejection separately from package-versus-reference exposure-label mismatch and releases the corrected interval only after both checks pass.
gap: Tchetgen Tchetgen--VanderWeele Section 4.3 gives Hoeffding-type finite-sample intervals for direct, indirect, total, and overall binary-outcome effects under two-stage partial interference, and Rigdon--Hudgens gives exact randomization-test inversions for those effects under stratified interference. Exposure-mapping papers give inverse weighting and asymptotic inference, while recent network minimax theory studies mean-squared error and often chooses the design. None treats fixed independent assignment on unequal cliques as a heterogeneous categorical erasure channel or lower-bounds the expected length of every uniformly valid randomized interval. The equal-block calculation cannot express simultaneous reveal probabilities, weights, or cap thresholds.
fill: The paper derives an observed-data block statistic and clipped Bernstein interval, supplies an exact Markov-kernel embedding that retains unrevealed assignment ancillaries and external randomization, and isolates the falsifiable posterior-spread inequality under the tilted sign laws as the sole no-dominance lower-bound bottleneck. It asks separately for a global equivalence between minimax length, the finite capped program, and trimming. Exact two-scale and six-block exhibits make the heterogeneous and saturation claims checkable. The version-pinned package diagnostic compares externally returned and independently recomputed labels, distinguishes graph rejection from label mismatch, and returns an interval only after equality is certified; equal blocks serve only as a reduction check.
